messages.subject: Error: Implementing Chinese Restaurant Process with CJS model
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to implement the Chinese Restaurant Process in my Cormack Jolly Seber (CJS) model. But I am getting an error while using the data where the individuals are captured for the first time in different years. I am not getting the error when all the individuals are captured for the first time in the same year. I attached a screenshot of my error here. 
Can you please help me with why I am getting this error? or if you can suggest to me any potential way out for dealing with these kinds of problems, that would e great.

Thank you for your time and I will really appreciate your help. 

Arjun

Hi,

I forgot to share my R-code, so here is my R-code for using DCRP in nimble.

library(nimble)
library(MCMCvis)

#########################################

h <- read.csv(file.choose(), header =T) # Capture Matrix

a <- read.csv(file.choose(), header =T) # Alive Matrix

N <- nrow(h)                            # Number of individuals

T <- ncol(h)                            # Number of sampling years

for (i in 1:T){
  names(h)[i]<- i
  names(a)[i] <- i
}

f_firth_m<-colnames(h)[max.col(h, ties.method = "first")]

first <- rep(NA, N)
for (i in 1:N){
  first[i]<- as.numeric(f_firth_m[i])   # Getting the first year of capture
}

#########################################

## Non-Parametric Capture-Recapture Model (CRP)
code <- nimbleCode({
 
  phi ~ dunif(0, 1)
 
  alpha ~ dgamma(2, 0.1)              
 
  xi[1:N] ~ dCRP(conc=alpha, size=N)  # Chinese Restaurant Process
 
  for(j in 1:M)   p[j] ~ dunif(0, 1)  # p for each subgroups
 
  for(i in 1:N) {
   
    for (t in first[i]:first[i]){
     
      a[i,t] <-1
    }
    for (t in (first[i]+1):T){
     
      mu1[i,t]<- (a[i,t-1]*phi)            
     
      a[i,t] ~ dbern(mu1[i,t])         # Alive at time t -> Alive at time t-1
     
      mu2[i,t] <- a[i,t]*p[xi[i]]      # DP on capture probability (p)
     
      h[i,t] ~ dbern(mu2[i,t])         # Capture at time t -> Alive at time t
    }
  }
})
M <- N   ## maximum number of subgroups
constants <- list(N=N, T=T, first=first, M=M)
data <- list(h=h, a=a)
inits <- list(phi=0.5, alpha=1, xi=rep(1,N), p=rep(0.5,M))
model_m1 <- nimbleModel(code, constants, data, inits)

McMC_m1 <- buildMCMC(model_m1, enableWAIC = TRUE)
compile_model_m1<- compileNimble(model_m1)
compile_MCMC_m1 <- compileNimble(McMC_m1, project = model_m1)
samples_m1 <- runMCMC(compile_MCMC_m1, niter = 10000, nchains = 2,
                      nburnin = 1000, thin = 10,summary = TRUE,
                      WAIC = TRUE)

waic <- samples_m1$WAIC

waic

#Model Summary
samples<- samples_m1$samples

MCMCsummary(samples,params = "p", round = 5)
MCMCsummary(samples,params = "phi", round = 5)

MCMCtrace(samples,pdf = F, ind = TRUE,
          Rhat = TRUE, n.eff = TRUE)



Please have a look and it will be great if kindly help me out. 

Arjun

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: Error: Implementing Chinese Restaurant Process with CJS model
parts:
Hi Arjun,

You're running into a limitation on how `dCRP` can be used based on how we do the sampling of the `xi[i]` values in the specialized CRP sampler.
The specific problem is that for those samplers to work, all the `xi[i]` nodes have to have the same number of dependent nodes, which isn't the case here because the individuals are first captured in different years. I can think of two separate options:

1) Use the stick-breaking representation discussed in the BNP chapter of the user manual to avoid the CRP sampler.

2) Write the code such that you start at year 1 for all individuals:
 for (t in 1:T){

mu1[i,t]<- (a[i,t-1]*phi)            
      a[i,t] ~ dbern(mu1[i,t])         # Alive at time t -> Alive at time t-1
      mu2[i,t] <- a[i,t]*p[xi[i]]      # DP on capture probability (p)
      h[i,t] ~ dbern(mu2[i,t])         # Capture at time t -> Alive at time t
    }

but then for individuals not captured until year `first[i]`, initialize their a[i,1],...,a[i,first[i]-1] for those years to be NA so that it is sampled as part of the MCMC and not treated as known. (And set their `h[i,t]` to indicate they were not captured in those years.)  I haven't fully thought this through, but hopefully that makes sense (both scientifically and is clearly described).

-Chris

parts:
Hi Arjun,

Note that "Error in if (cond) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed" appears in relation to the warning about model initialization. I suspect it's coming specifically from the fact that you have not initialized 'v'.

As far as the index out of bounds, please see our example for the stickbreaking specification in our manual (https://r-nimble.org/html_manual/cha-bnp.html#sec:exsb). In particular the output of `stick_breaking` is a set of probabilities not a set of category indicators, so it shouldn't be assigned to `xi`. So you'll need to fix up your model specification to correctly define `xi`.

As far as the -Inf logProb values, that is probably because you haven't initialized something. Please see this post from a while back where we talk about strategies for debugging cases like this by manipulating the model.

-Chris

library(nimble)
library(MCMCvis)

#########################################

h <- read.csv(file.choose(), header =T) # Capture Matrix

a <- read.csv(file.choose(), header =T) # Alive Matrix

N <- nrow(h)                            # Number of individuals

T <- ncol(h)                            # Number of sampling years

for (i in 1:T){
  names(h)[i]<- i
  names(a)[i] <- i
}

f_firth_m<-colnames(h)[max.col(h, ties.method = "first")]

first <- rep(NA, N)
for (i in 1:N){
  first[i]<- as.numeric(f_firth_m[i])   # Getting the first year of capture
}

#########################################

## Non-Parametric Capture-Recapture Model (CRP)
code <- nimbleCode({
 
  phi ~ dunif(0, 1)
 
  alpha ~ dgamma(2, 0.1)              
 
  xi[1:N] ~ dCRP(conc=alpha, size=N)  # Chinese Restaurant Process
 
  for(j in 1:M)   p[j] ~ dunif(0, 1)  # p for each subgroups
 
  for(i in 1:N) {
   
    for (t in first[i]:first[i]){
     
      a[i,t] <-1
    }
    for (t in (first[i]+1):T){
     
      mu1[i,t]<- (a[i,t-1]*phi)            
     
      a[i,t] ~ dbern(mu1[i,t])         # Alive at time t -> Alive at time t-1
     
      mu2[i,t] <- a[i,t]*p[xi[i]]      # DP on capture probability (p)
     
      h[i,t] ~ dbern(mu2[i,t])         # Capture at time t -> Alive at time t
    }
  }
})
M <- N   ## maximum number of subgroups
constants <- list(N=N, T=T, first=first, M=M)
data <- list(h=h, a=a)
inits <- list(phi=0.5, alpha=1, xi=rep(1,N), p=rep(0.5,M))
model_m1 <- nimbleModel(code, constants, data, inits)

McMC_m1 <- buildMCMC(model_m1, enableWAIC = TRUE)
compile_model_m1<- compileNimble(model_m1)
compile_MCMC_m1 <- compileNimble(McMC_m1, project = model_m1)
samples_m1 <- runMCMC(compile_MCMC_m1, niter = 10000, nchains = 2,
                      nburnin = 1000, thin = 10,summary = TRUE,
                      WAIC = TRUE)

waic <- samples_m1$WAIC

waic

MCMCsummary(samples,params = "p", round = 5)
MCMCsummary(samples,params = "phi", round = 5)

MCMCtrace(samples,pdf = F, ind = TRUE,
          Rhat = TRUE, n.eff = TRUE)
